Senses.PreferredTarget: a bean pops in cold ashes
AlternateTargets: a bean bursts in cold ash
Senses.Note: Event phrase, attributive person-label, and poetic heading all retain the same cold-ash image. They do not name different things. The family comparison with “dead ashes” (死灰), “cold ashes” (寒灰), and “a withered tree flowers” (枯木開花) supports the contrast visible in the passages but not an imported psychological explanation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 忽有箇冷灰豆爆底人到來，如何接待？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (靈機禪師語錄). Lingji Xingguan is the exact actor: he asks how to receive a (冷灰豆爆) person.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上善拼命必死，壁立萬仞，縣崖撒手，及第還鄉；中善寒爐煙絕，冷灰豆爆，親知下落；下善步步踏著實地
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (赤松領禪師語錄). Chisong Daoling is the exact actor: his (上堂) enumeration includes (冷灰豆爆).

Occurrences.Kwic: 設若今日冷灰豆爆，便見條抽石筍，燄吐冰河，鐵樹開華，木人撫掌。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (天岸昇禪師語錄), winter-solstice public exchange and address. Tian'an Sheng is the exact speaker of the stored conditional statement: if today a bean explodes in cold ashes, stone shoots branch, flames rise from the frozen river, the iron tree flowers, and the wooden person claps.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一朝冷灰豆爆，驀地一聲，管取現成受用。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (入就瑞白禪師語錄), address at Weiyang Monastery while traveling to Baizhang. Ruibai Mingxue is the exact speaker: he directs listeners to investigate a critical phrase until one morning a bean explodes in cold ashes and, with a sudden sound, present use is assured.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師問眾：「枯木開花即不問，冷灰豆爆時如何？」定侍者云：「平地一聲雷。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (遠菴僼禪師語錄). Yuan'an Feng is the exact actor: (師問眾) introduces (冷灰豆爆時如何).

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 石霜云休去歇去一念萬年去寒灰枯木去古廟香爐去一條白練去冷秋秋地去
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source text (普濟玉琳國師語錄): Shishuang Qingzhu is the exact headword-bearing speaker or grammatical actor in the complete case.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 山僧也是慣向泠灶裏下火，不免將錯就錯，或死灰裏爆出一粒豆也不可知。
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Complete Record of Chan Master Tianjie Juelang Dasheng (天界覺浪盛禪師全錄): in his instruction to Chan student Huisheng, Juelang Dasheng says that he is accustomed to lighting a cold stove and that a bean might burst from dead ashes.

Senses.Explanation: Its recorded neighbors make the image concrete: “the cold furnace has no smoke; a bean pops in cold ashes” (寒爐煙絕，冷灰豆爆); a public question asks, “leaving aside a withered tree flowering, what about when a bean pops in cold ashes?” and receives “a thunderclap on level ground” (平地一聲雷). Other addresses follow the phrase with impossible growth—stone bamboo shoots sprout, flame comes from an icy river, an iron tree flowers, and a wooden man claps—or simply with “suddenly, one sound” (驀地一聲). The corpus also speaks of “a person in whom a bean has popped in cold ashes” (冷灰豆爆底人), making the image an appraisal in an interview. Zen bends a domestic image of an unlikely pop from spent ash into a stock address and interview phrase, repeatedly paired with sound and impossible renewal. Those pairings are the texts’ own; this entry assigns no hidden event to the image.
